content.name: Content Placeholder 2
paragraphs: How can we collect and store large amounts of data?
By building tools and data structures to efficiently index and serve data
How can we efficiently query data?
By compiling high-level declarative queries into efficient low-level plans
How can we safely update data?
By managing concurrent access to state as it is read and written
How do different database systems manage design trade-offs?
e.g., at scale, in a distributed environment?

paragraphs: A data model is a collection of concepts for describing data
The relational model of data is the most widely used model today
Main Concept: the relation- essentially, a table
A schema is a description of a particular collection of data, using the given data model
E.g. every relation in a relational data model has a schema describing types, etc.

content.name: Title 1
paragraphs: Transactions

content.name: Content Placeholder 2
paragraphs: A key concept is the transaction (TXN): an atomic sequence of db actions (reads/writes)
If a user cancels a TXN, it should be as if nothing happened!
Transactions leave the DB in a consistent state
Users may write integrity constraints, e.g., ‘each course is assigned to exactly one room’

content.name: TextBox 3
paragraphs: Atomicity: An action either completes entirely or not at all

content.name: TextBox 8
paragraphs: Consistency: An action results in a state which conforms to all integrity constraints

content.name: Rectangle 9
paragraphs: However, note that the DBMS does not understand the real meaning of the constraints– consistency burden is still on the user!

content.name: Title 1
paragraphs: Challenge: Scheduling Concurrent Transactions

content.name: Content Placeholder 2
paragraphs: The DBMS ensures that the execution of {T1,…,Tn} is equivalent to some serial execution
One way to accomplish this: Locking
Before reading or writing, transaction requires a lock from DBMS, holds until the end
Key Idea: If Ti wants to write to an item x and Tj wants to read x, then Ti, Tj conflict.  Solution via locking:
only one winner gets the lock
loser is blocked (waits) until winner finishes

content.name: TextBox 3
paragraphs: A set of TXNs is isolated if their effect is as if all were executed serially

content.name: Rectangle 9
paragraphs: What if Ti and Tj need X and Y, and Ti asks for X before Tj, and Tj asks for Y before Ti?
-> Deadlock!  One is aborted…

content.name: Rectangle 10
paragraphs: All concurrency issues handled by the DBMS…

content.name: Title 1
paragraphs: Ensuring Atomicity & Durability

content.name: Content Placeholder 2
paragraphs: DBMS ensures atomicity even if a TXN crashes!
One way to accomplish this: Write-ahead logging (WAL)
Key Idea: Keep a log of all the writes done.
After a crash, the partially executed TXNs are undone using the log

content.name: TextBox 3
paragraphs: Write-ahead Logging (WAL): Before any action is finalized, a corresponding log entry is forced to disk

content.name: Rectangle 9
paragraphs: We assume that the log is on “stable” storage

content.name: Rectangle 10
paragraphs: All atomicity issues also handled by the DBMS…
